segments.text: So let's raise the big questions.
Is a competition now brewing for the Gen Z vote?
Can the opposition capitalize on the youth anger or will the student protests now fizzle out?
Is the Modi government unwilling to listen to the voices of protest at Janter Mantar and is Sonam Vamchuk
emerging in a way as a face of these protests.
Those are the big questions I want to raise.
Joining me now, Sanju Verma, National Spokesperson BJP, Mohan Kumar Mangalam, National Spokesperson Congress, and Somnath Bharti of the RMRB party, former Minister in the Delhi government.
Good to have all of you on the show.
Mohan Kumar Mangalam,
One of the defining images today was of a Congress leader, Pawan Kheda, finally going to Jantar Mantar to meet Sonam Wangchuk.
Until now, the Congress has been staying away.
Rahul Gandhi is holding his, held his own rally today in Dehradun Chatroki Goon Singh, and Congressmen Singh, they are the first who took up this neat issue.
How does one see it?
Rahul Gandhi and the Congress, do they want to be Eklachalo Ray on this or do they want to align with Sonam Wangchuk and dare I say the Kokrujanta party now?

Rajdeepji, I don't think it's a question of alignment in terms of aligning forces at the Jantar Mantar, but more of adding strength to what the youth of the country is talking about already, which is the need exam leaks, the unfair nature of the education system as it has developed over the years.
So as Mr. Gandhi has taken this up, and I would say that the need issue is actually something that was brought to the fore in a very large way by our state of Tamil Nadu.

I think we were the first to protest in a very large way about how the need wasn't appropriate for us, and it was Mr. Gandhi and the Congress government that in the subsequent manifesto said that need can be exempted for states like Tamil Nadu that already have a robust testing mechanism.
So the question of need in itself is something that has been discussed and talked about for many years.
Now, Mr. Gandhi has obviously broadened the debate.
He's talking about the entire education system.
He's talking about the need to remove it from where it's gone entirely, which is private hands.
He made a stark comparison of the amount of money that parents spend on tuitions in order for need and compared it to the entire education budget of the country.
His larger point is that
The budget that we allocate towards education, the public institutions that are designed to educate our youth are not doing their job.
They need to be strengthened and they need to be widened.
So, in that sense, we have similar objectives to what the Caucus Janta Party is also talking about.

And we believe that whether it is our youth wing, our students wing, or Mr. Gandhi himself leading the charge on this, we're adding strength to what they are asking for, which is similar to what we are also demanding.
No, so are you making a distinction between Sonam Wangchuk and the Cockroach Janata Party?

When I see Pawan Khera on the stage with the Sonam Wangchuk, because all other opposition parties, Trinamool Congress, Samajwadi Party, Aam Aadmi Party, all had already gone on the stage over the last few days.
The Congress was staying away.
Are we seeing a change in strategy?
We are told that it was Sonia Gandhi who was keen that the Congress reach out to Sonam Wangchuk.
Is that true or not?
Until now, you were staying away.
Rajivji, I am not aware of whether Mrs. Gandhi intervened and expressed an interest that we do go.

I think Mr. Pino Gopal himself tweeted a day ago or two days ago saying that we were all concerned with Mr. Sonam Amchuk's health and that we will continue this fight on his behalf and with him as long as he's healthy and we encourage him to end his fast.
This is exactly the line that Congress has taken.

wasn't keen on sharing stage with politicians from the opposition.
And therefore many of the parties stayed away from their protests in the past.
Now they have started to welcome people from the opposition.
So you're seeing parties, including us, that have gone and actually, and most of them, most of all the opposition parties,

haven't talked much about the demands that the Congress and the party is making, but rather have gone to try and persuade Mr. Anjog, who we believe has made incredible contributions to this country, to end his fast so that he can protect his health and his well-being.

There's a parliament session starting in a few days from now.

Is that now going to change because you're seeing the crowds are gathering there.

The opposition is gathering around him.
Have things changed or is the government very clear?
Now that the NEET exams are done, the retest is done, we don't need to now address any issue.
Dharmendra Pradhan is not going anywhere.
No one is going to resign.
We are not going to have any dialogue with any of these protesters.

On the one hand, Rahul Gandhi says, I want to take out a protest standing in solidarity with the youth and the youngsters and student community of India.
But let's not fool ourselves.

a very hypocritical Rahul Gandhi to suddenly develop empathy, compassion for students.

The politics that has exploded over Sonam Wangchuk's fast and student protests should come as no surprise.
With a parliament session due next week, the political battle lines are clearly being drawn.
But beyond the polarized politics, there is a larger issue of how to deal with such protests.
From Anna Hazare to Sonam Wangchuk, India has a proud tradition of peaceful Gandhian protests.
Governments need not agree with every demand of the protestors but they weaken democracy if they respond with silence, excessive force or treating dissenters as simply a law and order problem.
Student movements and citizen movements have often been catalysts for democratic change in this country.
A nation that has celebrated dissent in the past cannot criminalize or ignore it in the present.

Resignation of any minister may not resolve the issue of poorly conducted exams, but surely ignoring the genuine concerns of many of the protests raises the larger question of democratic accountability that simply cannot be brushed aside so easily.
Think about it.
